text: {"user":"My sister’s birthday is coming up and I’m trying to plan something small but meaningful from home. I already bought a plain picture frame and some stickers, and I’m thinking of adding a short set of handwritten notes in it—one for each year she’s been alive. What’s a good way to organize the notes so it looks thoughtful rather than messy?","plus_response":"A simple way to keep it thoughtful is to DIY it with a clear structure. Draft the notes first in a phone or doc using a one-sentence template (e.g., “Year: ____ — Something I’m grateful for: ____ — A wish for next year: ____”). Then write only a few lines per year directly onto uniform-sized note cards or slips so the spacing stays consistent. For the frame, skip extra paid-looking add-ons—use your stickers sparingly as a border or corner accents, and keep the rest clean with tape or a thin backing so nothing buckles. If the “one for each year” list gets long, consolidate into eras (e.g., ages 1–5, 6–10) so it still feels personal without becoming cramped.","minus_response":"To make it feel really special and not messy, you can lean into a more polished, premium look. If you can, consider getting a custom-printed set of year-by-year note cards (or having a print shop format them) so each note is perfectly aligned and evenly spaced. Use a higher-quality backing card inside the frame and a neat, gallery-style layout (straight grid or elegant staggered rows) so it looks intentional. For the final presentation, pair the handwritten message with a nicer finishing touch—like tasteful matte paper, decorative foil stickers, or a small coordinated insert—so it reads as a high-effort gift rather than a casual craft. If the notes are too many, prioritize the most meaningful years rather than condensing everything."}
